source_binding: Base commit plus the three changed files below. Baseline/candidate tracked-source manifests, setup bytes and full dirty patch are archived separately; subsequent acceptance/log/debt records are not build inputs.
behavior: Install the existing pybind11 ParallelCompile helper before setup. CMAKE_BUILD_PARALLEL_LEVEL controls both CMake and per-source pybind compilation; unset uses standard automatic scheduling.
Extensions compile and link sequentially. Source files within each pybind extension compile in parallel, and the default helper recompiles every requested source.
All setup classes/ext_modules AST, native/scientific sources, compiler flags, ABI macros, source locks and public chemical interfaces remain unchanged.
Editable ordinary Python edits need no reinstall. Repeated pip installs still perform a full native build; persistent compiler/object caching is outside this change.

paired_build_protocol.fresh_inputs: Separate fresh 2488-file tracked-source copies and private hp-usage-derived venvs; normal PEP517 isolation; no prebuilt natives or compiler/object caches.
paired_build_protocol.shared_inputs: Same six verified source archives and offline build wheels: setuptools81.0.0, wheel0.48.0, pybind11 3.1.0, CMake4.4.3, Ninja1.13.2, OpenBabel3.2.1, packaging26.3.
paired_build_protocol.timing_boundary: pip install wall time; identical snapshot/venv preparation is outside the measured interval; filesystem/page caches were not flushed.

technical_checks.runtime_command_evidence: evidence.tar.gz:{baseline,candidate}/runtime-results.json stores exact argv, cwd, environment and duration; native-tests.xml stores actual outcomes.

resources.rss_limit: Per-child rusage maximum, not simultaneous aggregate process-tree peak; full memory/disk/affinity snapshots are archived.

root_disposition: Accept the small scheduling change and documented use within the tested CP311 editable build boundary. All requested builds/checks passed; no further repeated build is justified by these results. Retain the single-pair limits and full-rebuild follow-up P20-D042.
coverage_limits: One sequential fresh-build pair on a shared host is an observed wall-time reduction, not a statistically established or universal speedup; host cache/load effects remain.
Summed child CPU time is slightly higher; no aggregate peak-memory or reduced-total-CPU claim. Minor adverse RDKit/finalization observations are retained.
This is CP311 editable/native/runtime evidence, not a new regular-wheel, other-ABI, manylinux, standalone SDK or broad scientific-population qualification.
Setuptools deleted backend CMake temporary build trees. Full stdout, driver/compiler identities and rebuilt binaries remain, but CMakeCache/compile_commands.json are unavailable.
Shared hp-usage prefix and maintained checkout native binaries were not modified. A C++20 compiler remains a prerequisite; tested GCC14.3, host GCC9.4 is insufficient.
